questions.qtext: Which of the following statements is/are correct?

options.text: The intersection of two recursive enumerable language is recursive enumerable.
Recursive enumerable languages closed under union and complements.
Recursive language is closed under positive closure.
Recursive language is closed under inverse homomorphism.

questions.solution:
(a, c, d)
• Recursive enumerable languages are closed under union and intersections. But not complement.
• Recursive language are closed under positive closure and inverse homomorphism.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statements are correct?

options.text: Emptyness property of a DCFL is not decidable.
Finiteness property of a CFL is not decidable.
The union of two deterministic context free language is deterministic context free.
The complement of a deterministic context free language is recursive.

questions.solution:
(d)
• Emptyness property of DCFL is decidable.
• Finiteness property of CFL is decidable.
• DCFL is not closed under union.
• DCFL are closed under complement, hence recursive too.

questions.qtext:
Which of the following problem are decidable?
I. Equivalence problem in recursive enumerable languages.
II. Co-finiteness problem in deterministic context free language.
III. Intersection finiteness problem in Turing Machine.
IV. Subset problem in regular language.
questions.solution:
(b)
• Equivalence problem is undecidable problem in REL.
• Co-finiteness problem is decidable problem in DCFL.
• Intersection finiteness problem is undecidable problem in TM.
• Subset problem is a undecidable problem in regular language.

questions.qtext:
Consider the below statement about Rice theorem.
I. Rice theorem can be used to show that a language is decidable.
II. Rice theorem can be used to show that a language is undecidable.
III. Rice theorem implies that there are infinitely many undecidable languages.
IV. Rice theorem implies that there are only finitely many undecidable languages.
The number of the above correct statements is/are ________.

NAT
questions.solution:
2
• Statement 2 and 3 are correct, i.e., Rice theorem can be used to show that a language is undecidable.
• Rice theorem implies that there are infinitely many undecidable languages.
